headline: This change puts your live Stripe payment key into the code and the shared files, so do not ship it as it stands.
what_changed: A new settings file was added. It holds your live Stripe secret key (the master password to your Stripe account), your public Stripe key and your site address.
The rule that kept settings files like this out of the shared project history was removed. The new file will now be saved and shared with everyone who can see the code.
The checkout code now has the live secret key typed directly into it. It uses that key whenever the key setting is missing, for example on preview (test) versions of the site.
Before this change, the app refused to start if the key was missing. Now it quietly falls back to taking real payments with your live account, even on test versions.

risks.title: Live Stripe secret key written into the code
risks.explanation: Your live Stripe secret key now sits in plain text in two places. Anyone who can see the code can use it to take money, issue refunds, read customer payment details or change your account. That includes any developer, contractor or tool with access, and the whole internet if the code is ever public. Treat the key as leaked: create a new key in Stripe, cancel the old one, and remove it from both files before saving them.

risks.title: Safety rule protecting secret files was removed
risks.explanation: The project had a rule stopping settings files with secrets from being saved into shared history. This change deletes that rule. So this file, and any future one like it, will be saved and copied wherever the code goes. Once a secret is in the history, deleting the file later does not remove it. Put the rule back.

risks.title: Test versions of the site will take real payments
risks.explanation: Preview (test) versions of the site will now use your live account instead of failing. Anyone testing checkout there, staff included, will be charged real money. Those test orders will also mix with your real sales records. Preview versions should use Stripe's test key, set as a setting on the hosting service, and never fall back to the live key.

questions_for_developer: Can you create a new Stripe secret key, cancel the old one, and confirm the old one no longer works, since it is now in the code?
Can you remove the key from the checkout code and the new settings file, and put back the rule that keeps settings files out of the shared code?
Can you fix the preview (test) versions by adding Stripe's test key as a setting on the hosting service, so they never use the live account?
Has this code been pushed or shared anywhere yet? If so, the key is in that copy's history and must be treated as public.
good_news: The live secret key is only used by the server-side checkout code, not the pages customers' browsers load, so it is not sent to visitors directly.
The real problem, preview versions failing, is simple to fix the right way by adding a setting on the hosting service.
